roadmap_item: F3 (ring 1) — ambient fill; shadows stop crushing to black. Commissioned by corpus/90-verdicts/wave1/W1-VISUAL-BLIND-PROTOCOL-A-r1.md remedy R3, named by 3 of 5 blind judges.
baseline_pinned_reason: HAZARDS.md #12 — HEAD is not the baseline. Pinned before any edit this piece made. Verified this turn: `git log --oneline eafd1316 -1` is 'Roadmap: F2 is delivered on stills alone, and the directive asks for motion', i.e. F1 and F2 are ALREADY IN the baseline, and `git diff eafd1316 HEAD -- game/src/render/post/composite.js game/src/render/renderer.js` is 86 insertions / 1 deletion and is F3 and nothing else. So the delete-the-fix control removes F3 while leaving F1 and F2 standing. The two files as they stood at that sha are committed at corpus/90-verdicts/wave1/artifacts/W1-F3-AMBIENT-FILL/baseline-src/ so the control can be rebuilt on a GPU Pod that has no .git.
could_not_do: **THE HEADLINE, AND IT IS A FALSIFICATION OF MY OWN PIECE.** The delete-the-fix control on real hardware (RTX A4500) came back RED, and it was right to. The measurement this piece had been using — capture GI-off, then capture GI-on, compare — was run against the pinned pre-F3 tree, where the shader is physically absent and `setVisualFeature('giFill')` throws. It still produced p10_luma 4.641 then 14.353. The head tree produced 4.641 then 15.001. **9.712 of the head run's 10.360 'improvement' — 93.7% of it — is reproduced by a tree with no fix in it.** The first capture is identical on both trees to three decimals; only the second diverges. So the block-ordered instrument was measuring capture ORDER (something that settles between the first and second capture) and only marginally the shader. This is RULES rule 6's third and worst shape — an inert-looking fix whose number moves the right way anyway — and nothing except the delete-the-fix control would have caught it. Every SwiftShader number this piece reported before this point inherits the same confound and none of them should be cited.

MY FIRST NULL-CONTROL METRIC (falloff_ratio = p90/p10 of the whole crop) WAS THE WRONG OPERATIONALISATION OF 'DIRECTIONAL FALLOFF', FOUND BY RUNNING IT, NOT BY REASONING IN ADVANCE. A flat additive lift K, solved to match the real fix's shadow-floor lift, produced a HIGHER falloff_ratio than the real fix (4.00 vs 3.46). The ratio rewards moving p90 up alongside p10, which is the flattening a global lift does. Replaced with a direct p90-movement comparison at matched p10 and kept falloff_ratio as reported, non-gating context.

THE NULL CONTROL'S MATCHING CHECK WAS ALSO WRONG, AND ALSO FOUND BY RUNNING IT. It demanded the flat lift's p10 match the fix's within 0.5 luma. An 8-bit additive lift is quantised — for integer channel values round(px+K) = px+round(K) — so the achievable p10s are one luma apart and no K can land within 0.5 of an arbitrary target (measured: 4.734 -> 15.734 at K=11, target 15.116). Worse, the bisection over real K converged onto the discontinuity itself and the applied lift became whichever side floating point landed on, which made the algebraic cross-check disagree with the frame it was predicting (4.2986 predicted vs 4.4105 measured). Fixed by searching over integers only; the check now requires the control to receive at least the fix's lift and at most one quantum more, and the algebraic prediction now agrees to 1e-4.

`g.h()` FROM tools/lib/browser.mjs DOES NOT THROW ON AN IN-PAGE ERROR — it calls die() and exits the process (EXIT 12). The first version of the delete-the-fix arm wrapped `g.h('setVisualFeature', ...)` in try/catch to detect the fix's absence; that is dead code, and the control run died instead of recording the absence. The evaluate has to happen inside the page. Worth knowing for anyone writing a control that expects a harness call to be missing.

THE ORBIT/PAN MOTION SWEEP WAS BLOCK-ORDERED TOO (whole off sweep, then whole on sweep) and inherited the same confound. Its symptom in the hardware run: at the SAME orbit angle the two blocks' first captures came back 14.321 and 5.276, both outliers against their own neighbours, direction arbitrary. Rebuilt to take both arms at each pose before the camera moves.

TUNING, CARRIED FORWARD AND STILL TRUE: the shipped uGIStrength 0.22 / uGIRadius 1.0m / uGIMaxDist 0.4m measurably REDUCES local_contrast_med (hardware: 6.172 -> 4.328, ~30%). The bounce average is mechanically a soft blur of nearby lit colour, and averaging a wide neighbourhood into a very dark pixel washes out what little texture the base shading carried. `local_contrast_med` is one of the two statistics the original blind verdict used to corroborate the judges (5/5 named the reference on it), so moving it the WRONG way is a real cost and is named here rather than hidden. A shader that separated 'how much to lift' from 'how much to blur' would likely do better; out of scope for this pass.

F2's KNOWN TERRAIN-FACET ARTIFACT (derivative-based normals reading every low-poly facet as its own plane) was not investigated for interaction with the fill. Unmeasured, because the confound above consumed the measurement budget.

evidence.swiftshader: corpus/90-verdicts/wave1/artifacts/W1-F3-AMBIENT-FILL/sw-head/ (block design, confounded, kept for the record). SwiftShader and hardware agreed to within 0.1 luma on every still statistic, which is worth knowing for future pieces: for THIS metric the software renderer was not the weak link.

next_step: PENDING: the paired/alternating hardware run (reports/runpod-gpu/runs/w1-f3-paired/) decides whether the F3 shader has any real effect once capture order is controlled for. If the paired lift is large and collapses on the pinned-baseline clone, F3 stands on a sound measurement. If it is small, F3 does not stand and the honest report is that the shader is close to inert and the block numbers were an artifact.
